current_leader.name: Cloud support-plan right-sizing engine
current_leader.state_transition: monthly cloud spend and support-case/incident telemetry update -> current paid support tier cost is recomputed -> compare observed support need and risk against cheaper eligible tier -> recommend KEEP/DOWNGRADE/UPGRADE at the next permissible boundary -> verify support-fee delta
current_leader.why_survived: AWS paid support is explicitly monthly, percentage-of-gross-cloud-spend pricing with large minimums and tier discontinuities. Billing, support-case, incident and account telemetry are naturally machine-readable. AWS provides a pricing calculator and manual plan-change workflow, but current searches did not find a first-party or independent product that continuously combines actual support utilization/risk with projected spend to recommend the cheapest sufficient support tier.
current_leader.strongest_evidence: AWS Business Support+ is priced at the greater of $29/account or 9%/7%/5%/3% of monthly AWS charges; Enterprise Support is the greater of $5,000/month or 10%/7%/5%/3%; Unified Operations has a $50,000/month minimum. Paid plans are monthly, and AWS exposes plan-management workflows plus Support/Trusted Advisor APIs on paid tiers.
current_leader.closest_threat: AWS itself exposes plan comparison, pricing calculation and downgrade workflows; broad FinOps providers can absorb support-plan advice, and Enterprise downgrades require contacting the TAM. No exact continuous support-utilization-aware optimizer was found in this run.
current_leader.smallest_intervention: Read cloud billing forecast, current support tier, support-case history, incident/severity history and required support features; output KEEP/DOWNGRADE/UPGRADE plus deterministic next-month fee delta and risk/features lost. Do not change the plan automatically.
current_leader.monetization: Per verified plan-change event, low fixed monthly fee, or capped percentage of verified support-fee savings for a defined measurement window.
current_leader.biggest_unresolved_risk: Actual support-tier overprovisioning is not yet quantified, and support value is partly tail-risk insurance rather than observed ticket utilization; a simple annual review may capture much of the value.
current_leader.next_research_test: Attack leakage and competition: find evidence of enterprises materially overpaying for support tiers, determine how often the economically optimal tier changes, and search FinOps/MSP products specifically for continuous support-plan right-sizing. If over-tiering is mostly static or exact tooling exists, demote/reject.

runner_ups.note: Clean decision, but paid acceleration increasingly looks like rational working-capital demand; avoidable fraction remains unproven.
Programmable and measurable, but incremental savings beyond competent static tuning remain unproven.
Strong structural mechanism but still lacks a sufficiently valuable defensible vertical.

candidate_events.reason: Beats prior leader with larger deterministic recurring fee delta and cleaner non-invasive telemetry-driven decision; Gate 2/6/8 remain uncertain.
No new evidence of avoidable acceleration; willingness-to-pay evidence continues to support rational liquidity demand.

candidate_events.fatal_flaw: Exact products already automate vacancy tracking, tenant chargebacks, deposit recovery, utility allocation and vacant-cost recovery.
Exact SaaS-management products already correlate activity to entitlements and automatically reclaim idle seats.
Already-covered rejected family; fresh exact products continue to audit linehaul, fuel, accessorials, duplicates and shipment-state mismatches.

new_search_rules: Treat service/support tiers as programmable money flows when price is a recurring percentage/minimum and entitlement need can be inferred from independent usage/incident telemetry.
Do not equate low observed support usage with waste: support is partly tail-risk insurance; the counterfactual must include required response times/features and risk tolerance.
A first-party pricing calculator is not by itself Gate-8 failure if it does not continuously decide the economically sufficient tier from external/operational telemetry.
